cards.title: Use high-perceived-value, low-COGS gifts with purchase instead of discounts
cards.summary: Substitute or supplement discounts with gift-with-purchase items that feel valuable to the customer but cost the brand little.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to incentivize a first purchase or subscription while protecting margin.

cards.title: Organize offer testing by traffic source and margin
cards.summary: Structure offer creation as a system: first split by traffic channel, then by the two goals of more spend or more buyers, then check margin feasibility.
cards.use_when: Building a repeatable offer-testing calendar rather than improvising promos.

cards.title: A basic CRO and customer-data stack for a DTC store
cards.summary: Assemble a small stack for site speed, first-party data, heatmaps, custom page building, and customer identification.
cards.use_when: Choosing tools to support conversion optimization and first-party data collection on a Shopify-style store.

cards.title: Design mobile-first and account for dark mode
cards.summary: Assume most traffic is mobile and design the full experience—including email—for mobile and dark-mode viewing first.
cards.use_when: Designing PDPs, landing pages, and email templates for a store whose traffic is majority mobile.

cards.title: Judge email performance by revenue per recipient within segments
cards.summary: Track revenue per recipient (RPR) by cohort and segment rather than only at the list level, to see which audiences are worth sending to.
cards.use_when: Reporting on email/SMS performance and deciding which segments to prioritize or suppress.

cards.title: Map subscription churn peaks and intercept them
cards.summary: Understand the three churn peaks in a subscription (day one, ~day 28, and ~day 31–45) and deploy education and gifts to reduce them.
cards.use_when: Reducing subscription churn and building the post-purchase communications calendar.

cards.title: Pre-empt the four stated cancellation reasons with downgrades and alternatives
cards.summary: When subscribers cancel, they cite four reasons; build specific save paths for each instead of a generic discount.
cards.use_when: Designing cancellation flows and retention offers for subscription or repeat-purchase products.

cards.title: Send plain-text founder and team emails to build retention
cards.summary: Use plain-text, non-designed emails from the founder, support, and product team as a low-cost retention channel.
cards.use_when: Planning the monthly retention email calendar and deciding what non-promotional content to send.

cards.title: Run response-driven campaigns to improve deliverability and engagement
cards.summary: Prompt customers to reply or submit content so list engagement and inbox placement improve while generating user content.
cards.use_when: Trying to lift email engagement or sender reputation, or needing user-generated content for retention and social.

cards.title: Turn loyal customers into marketers with one-person asks
cards.summary: Convert high-value customers into advocates by making the ask small and achievable rather than viral.
cards.use_when: Building referral and word-of-mouth programs for repeat buyers.

cards.title: Fund a surprise-and-delight budget at the CX layer
cards.summary: Give customer service a discretionary budget to over-deliver on problems, because the perceived value of the product far outweighs its cost.
cards.use_when: Setting customer service policy and deciding how to handle damaged, missing, or unsatisfactory orders.

cards.title: Product selection: require repeat purchase, an emotional effect, and efficient packaging
cards.summary: Choose products that evoke a feeling or behavior change, support repeat purchase, and can ship in a small efficient parcel.
cards.use_when: Evaluating new product lines or SKUs for an ecommerce catalog.

cards.title: Product expansion: compete on format and effect, not just flavor
cards.summary: Differentiate by matching products to effects and occasions instead of adding more of the same flavor variation.
cards.use_when: Planning a product-line expansion or deciding how to position new SKUs on shelf and online.

cards.title: Build product feedback loops with post-purchase surveys and reviews
cards.summary: Capture first-time, repeat, and non-purchasers' input through post-purchase surveys, automated review requests, and follow-on outreach.
cards.use_when: Designing a process to feed customer data into product development, marketing, and sales outreach.

cards.title: Weigh building in public against key-man risk and stop-start effects
cards.summary: Publishing company metrics and founder content can lower CAC and open doors, but stopping it can reverse gains and creates key-person dependency.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether the founder or brand should publicly share metrics, revenue, and process content as part of acquisition and brand strategy.

cards.title: Build a personal content system: pillars, weekly debrief, no AI voice
cards.summary: Run a structured weekly content process around a few pillars, with human-written copy and past-performance analysis.
cards.use_when: Planning a founder-led content or social calendar that supports an ecommerce brand's acquisition.

cards.title: Route acquisition and spend decisions through people with media-buying experience
cards.summary: Understanding how to deploy paid spend without emotional attachment to the money is a durable skill that can drive both brand building and agency work.
cards.use_when: Deciding who should own paid acquisition, or whether to build a brand versus run media buying as a service.

cards.title: Reduce operating friction by non-negotiable morning routines
cards.summary: Deliberately delay caffeine and avoid email and breakfast early in the day to protect focus.
cards.use_when: Structuring a founder or operator workday around store and team demands.

cards.title: Evaluate 3PL and CX tooling for customer-experience dashboards, not just shipping
cards.summary: Prefer fulfillment partners with visibility into customer experience so service teams need fewer touchpoints to resolve issues.
cards.use_when: Choosing or renegotiating a 3PL or fulfillment partner.

cards.title: Six cash-conversion levers that gate bootstrap growth
cards.summary: Model DTC growth as a cash conversion cycle and diagnose which of six levers — CAC, AOV, maintained markup, return rate, sell-through, OpEx — is your current constraint before spending more on ads.
cards.use_when: You are planning next quarter's growth budget and deciding whether to spend more on acquisition or fix margins/inventory/Opex first

cards.title: Variable vs fixed expense rule: why OpEx cuts hit cash 1:1
cards.summary: The source's core accounting distinction: cutting fixed OpEx improves net income and net cash one-for-one, while cutting variable marketing spend does not.
cards.use_when: You are deciding where to cut to improve cash position without stalling revenue

cards.title: The 60-180 day lag on lever changes
cards.summary: Small financial-lever improvements rarely show up in a 30-day window; the compounding effect lands at 60-180 days in the net cash position.
cards.use_when: You are evaluating whether a CAC, AOV or margin change is working and deciding when to judge it

cards.title: Improving AOV without adding fixed cost
cards.summary: Raising AOV lifts revenue and gross profit while fixed marketing and OpEx stay flat, accelerating inventory turnover and shortening the cash cycle.
cards.use_when: You want faster cash turnover without increasing ad spend, e.g. on PDP, bundles or post-purchase upsells

cards.title: Maintained markup as an inventory-cash unlock
cards.summary: Raising MMU through supplier negotiation and on-site pricing cuts COGS and the stock needed for the same revenue, freeing cash even when the P&L gain looks modest.
cards.use_when: You are renegotiating supplier terms or repricing core SKUs and want to quantify the cash effect, not just the margin

cards.title: Returning-customer rate as the near-zero-CAC profit driver
cards.summary: The source argues returning customers generate 80-90% of net profit because reacquisition costs are minimal, so retention spend raises both net income and cash.
cards.use_when: You are allocating budget between acquisition and retention, or building post-purchase and lifecycle email flows

cards.title: Using 30-day sell-through to free trapped cash
cards.summary: Raising 30-day sell-through cuts the next inventory buy, releasing cash tied up in stock without changing revenue or gross profit.
cards.use_when: You are reviewing SKU range and open-to-buy and want to convert dead stock into cash

cards.title: The compounding lever strategy: move 2-3 levers at once
cards.summary: Adjusting two to three levers simultaneously — e.g. OpEx, MMU and sell-through — compounds into a much larger net cash position than any single fix.
cards.use_when: You are building a turnaround or growth plan and need to prioritise several financial fixes at once

cards.title: Model cash flow monthly, not just net income
cards.summary: A store can be net-income positive while its bank balance falls, because inventory purchases pull cash directly — so model the bank balance as well.
cards.use_when: You are reviewing monthly P&L and wondering why profit isn't showing up as cash, or sizing the next inventory buy

cards.title: Product research from Amazon review mining (True Classic method)
cards.summary: Use critical Amazon reviews of competitor products to find the fit, price and comfort problems worth building a first product around.
cards.use_when: Selecting your first hero product or overhauling an existing one, especially in apparel or another fit/sizing-sensitive category.

cards.title: Build 4-5 thumb-stop hooks per paid social ad
cards.summary: Test multiple opening hooks per creative concept because the first seconds decide whether the ad is seen at all.
cards.use_when: Producing paid social (Meta/other) ad creative and deciding how many variants to ship per concept.

cards.title: Shift spend from pure DR toward brand awareness and accept delayed attribution
cards.summary: Fund brand/podcast/live-event spend knowing its returns show up later in blended and survey data, not in same-platform ROAS.
cards.use_when: Deciding media mix and budget allocation once you have scale in direct-response, or when DR-only ROAS looks capped.

cards.title: Triangulate ecommerce attribution with post-purchase surveys
cards.summary: Use customer-reported discovery alongside platform data and business outcomes to investigate channel contribution.
cards.use_when: Reconciling reported ROAS/CAC across Meta, Google, Applovin and other channels, or deciding which channel actually deserves more budget.

cards.title: Cart architecture: multi-tier gift-with-purchase thresholds (True Classic example)
cards.summary: Set escalating spend thresholds in the cart that give progressively bigger gifts and nudge cross-category discovery.
cards.use_when: Setting cart/checkout offers, free-shipping thresholds or AOV-raising mechanics.

cards.title: Post-purchase upsell on already-authorized cards (AfterSell pattern)
cards.summary: Add a one-click post-purchase offer for high-margin items to capture extra revenue with no additional acquisition cost.
cards.use_when: Designing the post-purchase step, or looking for margin-efficient revenue after payment is captured.

cards.title: Simplify PDP and homepage to reduce exits
cards.summary: Remove navigational escape routes from product and home pages so shoppers stay in the purchase path.
cards.use_when: Structuring a product detail page or homepage layout, especially when bounce or exit rates are high.

cards.title: Fund inventory with supplier net terms instead of equity (True Classic example)
cards.summary: Negotiate vendor credit and safety stock to finance large inventory buys, preserving ownership but carrying real risk.
cards.use_when: Planning a big inventory commitment or deciding between raising capital and financing via suppliers.

cards.title: Welcome flow as the primary retention vehicle
cards.summary: Turn the post-purchase welcome email/SMS sequence into your main retention asset and split-test the discount depth.
cards.use_when: Designing post-purchase email/SMS, or trying to lift repeat purchase and LTV.

cards.title: Customer service 'wow budget' to reverse negative sentiment
cards.summary: Give CX a fixed budget to over-deliver on broken experiences so angry customers convert into promoters.
cards.use_when: Setting customer service policy or deciding how far to go to fix a bad order.

cards.title: Customer advisory group for product and merchandising feedback
cards.summary: Recruit high-LTV customers into a private group to give deep product and retail feedback.
cards.use_when: Planning new products, evaluating merchandising, or auditing retail presentation with real customers.

cards.title: Word-of-mouth and wild-bet stunts (poker chips, teacher wish lists, live gamification)
cards.summary: Small physical and philanthropic stunts can generate outsized word of mouth when they are genuinely notable or generous.
cards.use_when: Looking for low-budget awareness tactics beyond paid social, or planning a launch moment.
